Stephanie — thanks for the follow-up and for the deck. Quick answers and I’ve looped our procurement mailbox.

- Procurement lead: Maria Torres (procurement@lumina.ai). She handles vendor onboarding.
- Payment policy: Lumina requires a signed PO for any vendor relationship expected to exceed $10k/year. For small pilots under $10k we can consider corporate card, but our legal team wants vendor validation before prod access.
- Marketplace: AWS Marketplace is possible (we prefer consolidated billing there), but we’d need Redwood to be listed — that might take an extra 2–3 weeks.

I’m attaching a short PDF of our AP/process and a sample vendor checklist so you can confirm what you need to return. If you can accept a PO + Net30, that’s our most likely path.

Stephanie — quick recommendation: three pragmatic options ranked by speed to value:

Option A — Card pilot (fastest): if Lumina can make an exception for a sub-$10k pilot, we can start immediately. Requirement: valid CC on file and SOW signed. This avoids vendor onboarding delays.

Option B — PO + Net30 (standard): Accept PO and Net30. Requirements: signed PO, W9, COI, ACH remit info. We normally do light credit validation (verify legal entity + billing contact). We can provision a sandbox environment on receipt of PO and signed SOW; production dedicated capacity only after vendor validation is complete (~5–10 business days).

Option C — Marketplace (AWS): Best for organizations that insist on consolidated billing. Time to go-live depends on Redwood’s listing status; if we’re already listed it’s fastest, otherwise 2–3 weeks to enable.

Given what Alex said, recommended path: pursue Option B (PO + Net30) for formal purchase, but offer a limited trial (sandbox) on receipt of PO + signed SOW so they can start evaluation while onboarding finishes. For short-term momentum, ask if procurement will allow a one-time card charge for initial onboarding fees if they can’t start with a PO immediately.

I’ll draft a short mutual action plan you can send to Alex.

— Karthik

Hi Alex / Maria — thanks for the clarity. Based on your note and Karthik’s recommendation, proposed mutual action plan (MAP):

1) Lumina: Share signed PO (or purchase commitment email) by 2026-11-30, and send vendor onboarding docs (W9, COI, ACH remit).
2) Redwood: On receipt of PO + signed SOW we will provision sandbox access (hosted environment with token limits) within 48 business hours so your team can begin integration and quality testing.
3) Redwood: Complete vendor validation and fully enable invoicing/production provisioning within 5–10 business days of receiving required vendor docs.

If Lumina cannot provide a PO by 11/30 and still wants to start earlier, we can accept a one-time corporate card charge up to $7,500 against a signed SOW as an exception; otherwise the PO route is the primary path.

Attached: Redwood SOW and Vendor Packet to accelerate the process. Please confirm whether Lumina will proceed with the PO path or needs the temporary card exception and we’ll route paperwork accordingly. Happy to jump on a 15-min call with Maria to walk through the NAV and vendor docs if that helps.

Best — Stephanie Nguyen
